title: Keeping a Piece Covered by the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans in Good Standing
content:
The piece covered by a plan of the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans must be inspected at the interval the coverage sets, and an inspection counts only where it was logged on one of the channels the coverage recognises. An inspection is logged and coverage restored only while the plan stands at active, inspection overdue or suspended. Where no inspection is logged by the due date the plan falls out of good standing once the inspection grace in calendar days has run, and on the coverage that suspends for it coverage is then suspended. An inspection logged inside the restoration window puts the lapse right and coverage resumes from the day the inspection was logged, never retrospectively, so a loss that happened while the coverage was out of good standing stays refused. A finding that refers the piece to the bench does not by itself open a claim: the customer is told what was found and a claim is opened only if they ask for one. Where the restoration window has passed the plan is not restored and fresh coverage must be quoted, which the customer may decline.

## Standings at which an inspection is logged

| Standing of the plan under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans | An inspection may be logged and coverage restored |
|---|---|
| active | yes |
| inspection overdue | yes |
| suspended | yes |
| expired, cancelled, transferred, exhausted, quoted | no |

The standing is read from the plan record before the inspection is logged.

## Counter questions

**A piece is inspected at a store the coverage does not recognise for it. Does the inspection count?** No. An inspection counts only where it was logged on one of the channels that coverage recognises.

**Coverage was out of good standing for six weeks and a loss happened in week three. An inspection is now logged inside the restoration window. Is that loss answered for?** No. Coverage resumes from the day the inspection was logged and never retrospectively, so a loss that happened while the coverage was out of good standing stays refused.

**The inspection finds a stone loose and refers the piece to the bench. Is a claim now open?** No. The customer is told what was found, and a claim is opened only if they ask for one.
